common_name: Havana Yellow Lantana (Upright Golden Havana Series Lantana)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants after the last frost into full sun and well-drained soil, giving Havana Yellow's upright, well-branched habit room for good air movement.

directions: Golden-yellow flower clusters open continuously from late spring through fall on this heat-loving Dummen Orange introduction, drawing butterflies and other pollinators to Gulf Coast borders and large patio containers. Let soil dry between waterings once plants are established, since lantana rots quickly in soggy conditions, and skip deadheading because spent blooms are largely hidden by new flushes. Where winters drop below the mid-20s Fahrenheit, treat as a warm-season annual or bring potted specimens indoors before frost.

common_name: Little Lucky Peach Glow Lantana (Dwarf Early-Blooming Peach-Pink Lantana)

planting.note: Plant this dwarf, mounding selection after the last frost in full sun and lean, well-drained soil, spacing plants close together for a quick-filling edge or container planting.

directions: Bred to begin flowering roughly three weeks earlier than standard-sized lantana while staying under a foot tall, this Ball FloraPlant selection suits small containers, edging, and hanging baskets. Clusters of peach, pink, and soft-yellow blooms cover the compact plants from spring into fall, drawing butterflies while largely escaping deer browsing. Water sparingly once established, since like other lantanas this selection is markedly drought- and heat-tolerant and prone to root rot in wet soil, and it is reliably perennial only in the warmest zones, so gardeners further north should grow it as an annual or overwinter cuttings indoors.
